# no-bare-urls

- ID: `MD034`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `links`, `url`

Outside code and HTML, URLs and email addresses sit in angle brackets or links.

## Why

Some Markdown parsers do not turn a bare URL or email address into a link.

## Options

This rule has no options.

## Fix

The fix wraps the URL in angle brackets. gomdlint reports a URL without a fix
when parsers may disagree about where it ends, such as in a table, right after
an emphasis marker or with an \& in it. It also reports a www\. address without
a fix, because angle brackets do not make it a link. gomdlint may report a
finding without a fix when the fix would change a line with one character in
brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line,
because it could add or remove a task list checkbox.

## Configure

Under `rules`, `no-bare-urls: false` turns the rule off and
`no-bare-urls: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-bare-urls` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-bare-urls -->
```
